gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Rev-A-Shelf's per-shelf ratings for its kidney lazy susans (25 / 50 / 64 / 84 lb for 18 / 24 / 28 / 32 in) all work out to one rating of 20 lb per square foot. That means a shelf's capacity grows with the square of its diameter: dropping one size from 28 in to 24 in loses about 22% of capacity, and an 18 in shelf holds 30% of what a 32 in shelf holds.
standout_why: I compared against tidystow sizing-placement (cited in both chats), lily-bearing hardware guide, 4stnotary best-lazy-susan and simplehomenest lazy-susan-for-cabinet. Tidystow gives only a generic '15 and 50 pounds' for home turntables and says a turntable 'an inch too small loses a little capacity'. Lily lists bare-bearing ratings by size (6 in steel = 500 lb) but gives no shelf rating. 4stnotary states one rating (Eichzer 70 lb) and doesn't say what it means. Simplehomenest gives no ratings. None of them shows that the cabinet-shelf ratings are area-based. None warns that a bare-bearing figure like the 400 lb on the 6 in Everbilt plate ChatGPT showed can't be compared with a shelf rating.
decides: This changes how a shopper sizes a corner unit. Tidystow's rule is to go smaller if you're between sizes, but with Rev-A-Shelf polymer kidney shelves that costs capacity by area, not 'a little': 64 lb down to 50 lb per shelf from 28 in to 24 in. Buy the largest diameter the opening allows. For heavy items (cans, bottles) at a given diameter, Dowell's wood 18 in round shelf (50 lb per shelf) is rated at about 28 lb per sq ft against Rev-A-Shelf polymer's 20. The 400 lb Everbilt bearing figure is for the bare plate. It tells you nothing about how much a finished shelf will hold.

findings.note: The almond version of the same shelf reads 'This unit holds 20 lbs. Per Square Foot'. My arithmetic: a kidney shelf is a 270° circle (Dowell names its kidney line '270 Degree'), so area = 0.75·π·r². 18 in: 1.325 sq ft × 20 = 26.5 lb (stated 25). 24 in: 2.356 sq ft × 20 = 47.1 lb (stated 50). 28 in: 3.207 sq ft × 20 = 64.1 lb (stated 64). 32 in: 4.189 sq ft × 20 = 83.8 lb (stated 84). The per-shelf figures are the area rating applied to each size.
